body_markdown.description:
The reading copy of an HTML body, present exactly when
`message.body_markdown` is.

items.description:
One block of a Markdown body, as data a template can lay out. The Review page is rendered inside AFUI's restricted template environment, where no filter or value may carry pre-rendered markup. So the body is not turned into HTML here; it is turned into this tree, and the template writes the `

` and `` itself with ordinary autoescaping.

marker.description: A list item's bullet or number, e.g. `•` or `3.`.

items.description:
A run of text with one style. `href` is present only for `http`, `https`
and `mailto` targets; any other link scheme is shown as its text alone.

The last run of a link also carries what a person needs to judge it
without following it: `host`, the registrable domain the link really goes
to, and whether that is the sender's own domain.

host.description: Registrable domain (or bare host) of `href`, on the link's last run.

sender_domain_match.description:
Whether `host` is the sender's registrable domain. One rule, no
heuristics: equal or not. Absent when the sender's domain is unknown.

authentication.description:
Structured view of a message's `Authentication-Results` headers.

afmail does not classify mail; this only reports what the receiving server
asserted (which domain authenticated, and whether it aligns with `From`).
Pass authenticates the *domain*, not the legitimacy of the contents.

alignment.description:
Whether the DMARC-authenticated domain lines up with the visible `From`
domain. `Unknown` when there is nothing authenticated to compare against.

dkim.description:
Result of a single email authentication mechanism (SPF / DKIM / DMARC).

`Missing` means no `Authentication-Results` entry for the mechanism was
present at all — which is a distinct, and arguably more suspicious, state
than an explicit `none`.

dmarc.description:

body_markdown.description:
Markdown made from the HTML part for reading: links keep their text and
target, images become their alt text, structure becomes paragraphs,
lists and quotes. Present only when the message has an HTML part;
`body_text` stays the verbatim plain-text source that hashes and
quote segmentation are computed over.

contact.description:
Exact contact frontmatter associated from the sender address at
render/materialize time. Read-only on `message show`; refreshed when the
canonical contact changes, or by `afmail render refresh`.

human_suggestion.description:
A person's settled disposition of one message.

`based_on_agent_suggestion_uid` is `None` when the person originated this
disposition themselves rather than answering a proposal — the only case
where that is legal is `outcome: Decided`. Three invariants hold for every
value that reaches disk, checked right after deserialization rather than
left to each writer to remember:

1. `Decided` ⇒ `based_on_agent_suggestion_uid` is `None` and
   `suggested_action` is `Some`;
2. `Accepted` / `Changed` ⇒ `based_on_agent_suggestion_uid` is `Some`;
3. `Rejected` ⇒ `reason` is `Some`.

outcome.description:
A person's disposition of one Agent-suggestible item.

`Accepted` and `Changed` answer a proposal the Agent made; `Rejected` says
no (with a reason, whether or not there was a proposal to say no to);
`Decided` is the person originating a disposition the Agent never
suggested. There is no "deferred" or "submitted" value: silence about an
item just means it has not been settled yet, and a person can settle it,
and resettle it, at any time. See [`MessageHumanSuggestion`] for the
invariants each value carries.

origin.description:
Provenance tag for messages whose archived status comes from a remote
source rather than an explicit local disposition (e.g. "imap-archive").
